mail.description: one letter's envelope, sent or received

to.description: the address it is written to — absent when `deliver.to` names the recipient as an entity instead

at.description: when it was written, or when it arrived

target.description: the entity this letter is about — any entity at all, so correspondence hangs off the thing it concerns

message_id.description: the Message-ID other mail systems know this letter by — written from what arrived, and what a reply threads on

verified.description: whether the sending domain signed for this letter (DKIM) — false is recorded, never dropped: a letter nobody signed for is still a letter, and the reader is the one who decides what to trust

in_reply_to.description: the Message-ID this letter answers, exactly as the header wrote it — what arrives before `reply_to` can name an entity, and all a reply to a letter nobody kept ever has

sent_id.description: the id the sending service returned when it accepted this letter — written by whoever sent it, and what a delivery report is looked up by

email.description: an address, as an entity — what a person is reachable at

deliver.description: who a letter is for, as an entity in your graph

to.description: the recipient — their address is looked up when the letter goes out

tried.description: when the letter was handed to the sender — one with this and no outcome may have left, so it is never handed over again

delivered.description: the letter left: half of the outcome pair

via.description: how it went — the id the sender returned, or the address it went to

bounced.description: the letter did not leave: the other half

reason.description: what went wrong, as the sender reported it

notified.description: a recipient was told about something

inbox_list.title: List the inbox
inbox_list.description: List mail messages addressed to one reader and not yet archived, newest first: routed to them, written to them, or delivered to an email address they have. `●` marks unread, `·` read, `×` archived. Archiving is the only thing that removes a message from the list, so an empty inbox is one the reader emptied. Returns the message records as bundles (JSON objects with entity ids and component fields), up to limit (50 by default). Omit who for the caller; all: true includes archived messages.

who.description: whose inbox to read (default: the caller); pass its id or registered name

all.description: include archived messages, which is how to find anything hidden

limit.description: return at most this many messages (default 50)

inbox_archive.title: Archive an inbox item
inbox_archive.description: Remove one item from the inbox. Nothing is deleted and no history is lost: `inbox_list(all: true)` (CLI: `inbox list --all`) still shows it, and a later message on the same thread arrives as its own item. Returns the applied changes as bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components (named groups of fields) written or removed.

item.description: the item to archive; any entity an inbox can hold; pass its id or registered name

mail_show.title: Read a mail message
mail_show.description: Return one mail message in full: its headers, its body, and one-line summaries of the rest of its thread, with this message marked. The text is returned in content.body alongside the opened mark. Reading marks the message opened, which is why this tool writes where graph_show only reads.

letter.description: the message to read; pass its id or registered name

mail_reply.title: Reply to a mail message
mail_reply.description: Write a reply threaded on one message and request that it be sent. It is addressed to the other side of the original (the sender of a received message, or the recipient of one you sent) from the address the original used, with the subject prefixed `Re:`. Replying to a received message archives it: a thread you have answered is not waiting on you. The configured sender delivers it; a graph with no sender configured records the reply and never sends it. Returns the applied changes as bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components (named groups of fields) written or removed. Confirm the recipient and message before requesting delivery; a sent email cannot be recalled.

letter.description: the message being replied to; pass its id or registered name

mail_send.title: Send a mail message
mail_send.description: Create a mail message and request that it be sent. `to` is an email address or the id of an entity in this graph; an address nobody in the graph has becomes a new `email` entity, so the address book grows as mail is sent. `from` defaults to the caller’s own email address. Without a configured sender, the message is recorded but not sent. A configured sender delivers it asynchronously and writes `delivered` or `bounced` onto the message. Returns the applied changes as bundles: JSON objects with entity ids and the components (named groups of fields) written or removed. Confirm the recipient and message before requesting delivery; a sent email cannot be recalled. The initial result is not a delivery receipt; read the message again to check its outcome.

to.description: an email address, or the id of the entity it is for

from.description: the address it is sent from (default: the caller’s own)

about.description: the entity this message is about, so the correspondence is attached to it; pass its id or registered name

mail_check.title: Check the mail
mail_check.description: Check that every received mail message has a sender. Also reports incomplete configuration for a sender this server has configured. A message with a Message-ID but no `from` can never be answered, since a reply has no address to go to. Takes no arguments. Returns a report in content.body, with warning or failure findings when present; it does not repair the records or configuration.
